data.name: Jaiwanti
data.gender_notes: Jaiwanti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jaiwanti is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Jai' meaning victory and 'wanti' meaning desire. In Hindu mythology, Jaiwanti is the name of a goddess who embodies the desire for victory. She is believed to grant success and prosperity to those who worship her. The name Jaiwanti carries the meaning “Victory brings desire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jaiwanti usually hope their child will grow to embody victory brings desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodies the desire for victory and success in spiritual pursuits.
data.etymology: Jaiwanti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory brings desire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jaiwanti total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

The name Jaiwanti is a constant reminder of this and serves to inspire and motivate individuals to strive for success and excellence in all aspects of life. Jaiwanti was a legendary queen of the Malwa region in central India. She is credited with the establishment of the Chitra Kingdom and is remembered for her wisdom, courage, and generosity. Her name 'Jaiwanti' is derived from 'Jaya' meaning victory and 'Vanti' meaning generous or bestower.
